newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to speed up Big Three banks' privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to speed up Big Three banks' privatisation.

text.p: The Taiwan provincial government on Wednesday gave details of a long-planned sale of equity in the island's "big three" state-run banks, shortening the time for the effort to 14 months from 18 months.
The three banks are First Bank, Hua Nan Bank and Chang Hwa Bank.
A privatisation panel of the provincial government decided to release 15.9 percent of First Bank's shares, 7.5 percent of Hua Nan's and 4.6 percent in Chang Hwa's, state radio said.

The plan requires final approval from the Provincial Assembly, after which a date for the sale could be announced. Once begun, the privatisation would take 14 months to complete, four months less than originally planned.
The panel set no underwriting prices, saying it would let the market determine the banks' share values, the radio said.
After the share sale, government holdings would fall to 46 percent of First Bank, 45 percent of Hua Nan, and 37.83 percent of Chang Hwa, the report said.
Analysts have said reducing the government's stakes to below 50 percent should be regarded as privatisation. It was not known if there plans for further sales of state equity.
Share prices of the three banks were mixed at the close of trading on Wednesday.
First Bank ended down T$1 at T$114, Hua Nan rose 50 cents to T$103.50 and Chang Hwa lost T$1.50 to T$111.50.
